title: Power BI service basics: key concepts and terms

claims.text: Activity in the Power BI service splits into two roles: designers/creators who build, organize, and publish content, and consumers/business users who view, filter, and drill into that content to make decisions.

A semantic model (the renamed concept formerly called a dataset) is the container of modeled data that Power BI reports, dashboards, and apps are built on, and a single semantic model can combine multiple data sources.
A Power BI report is one or more pages of interactive visuals, text, and graphics that draw from exactly one semantic model, typically organized around a specific set of questions.

A Power BI dashboard is a single screen composed of tiles — interactive visuals, text, and graphics — used to monitor key metrics at a glance; unlike a report, it is one screen and can surface tiles sourced from multiple reports and models.
A Power BI app bundles dashboards, reports, and semantic models into a single package for distribution to individuals, groups, or a whole organization.
Publishing an app is the preferred way for designers to distribute related dashboards and reports to a large audience, instead of sharing items one at a time.

Workspaces are collaborative containers where designers manage collections of dashboards, reports, and other items; access is controlled through the Admin, Member, Contributor, and Viewer roles, and in Fabric the same workspace can also hold lakehouses, notebooks, and other Fabric item types.

A capacity is a dedicated set of compute resources backing Power BI content; Power BI Premium (P SKUs) and Fabric capacities of F64 or larger allow users on a free license to consume shared content, and a capacity is also required to use Copilot.

Copilot in Power BI — an AI assistant for building reports, analyzing data, and generating natural-language summaries — is enabled by default but only functions on a paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher, or Power BI Premium P1 or higher.
Excel workbooks uploaded to the Power BI service can be viewed directly or used as data sources feeding reports and dashboards.
Dataflows in the Power BI service are now designated legacy; they store reusable, centralized data-preparation steps, with Fabric's Dataflows Gen2 as the platform-level successor.
